Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 68, English)
Siya Tattva Sadhna: Darshan, Symbolism, and Everyday Miracles — A Live ExperienceSharing Round

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn satsang session structur ed almost entir ely as a r ound-r obin experience-sharing session, following practitioners' individual Siya T attva (Sita-element) sadhna sessions (explicitly r eferenced as the thir d and fourth sessions in this specific practice track). Unlike most sessions in this series, this transcript contains very little dir ect doctrinal teaching fr om Bhaiya — instead, its cor e content is a sequence of named practitioners' first-person accounts of their sadhna experiences, which Bhaiya r eceives, affirms, and occasionally contextualizes. Because this session is structurally almost entir ely live sangat interaction, it is pr ocessed as a full 3-part document, with an adapted Part I that documents the practice context and the recurring experiential patterns acr oss these testimonies rather than a conventional number ed-doctrine teaching.
1. Session Context: The Siya Tattva Sadhna Track

This session is an experience-sharing round following a specific ongoing sadhna practice called Siya Tattva sadhna (centered on the Sita element). Multiple practitioners explicitly reference which session number they are on — this particular round follows the third Siya Tattva session for some practitioners and the fourth for others, indicating this is a multi-part, sequential practice track rather than a single standalone exercise. One practitioner references a specific phase where "teenon ek saath" (all three phases together) was introduced as a new instruction partway through the track.
2. The Session's Format: Individual Testimony , Not Lectur e

Rather than delivering new doctrinal content, Bhaiya spends this session calling on practitioners one at a time (frequently opening with "kaisi ho, bahen?" / "kaise ho, bhai?") to share what they experienced during that day's (or recent) sadhna sessions, responding to each with brief af firmation, encouragement, or light clarification, and occasionally correcting a practitioner's uncertainty about their own experience (for example, confirming that reaching a state mistaken by a spouse for "falling asleep" was actually deep samadhi).
3. Recurring Physical Sensations Reported Across Multiple Accounts

Several practitioners independently reported similar physical sensations during their sadhna, including: intense warmth or heat (one practitioner described feeling "as if sitting in a furnace," another felt their face and ears grow hot along with a "boom boom" ener gy sensation), a pulsing sensation in the head compared to a heartbeat, pre-breakthrough shivering or chattering teeth that resolved once prayer/jaap began, and a persistent feeling of warmth in the hands/body despite genuinely cold ambient conditions (one practitioner specifically noted being in Himachal Pradesh, where it was cold, yet feeling no cold at all during the sadhna).
4. Recurring Visionary (Darshan) Patterns

Across the shared testimonies, a consistent set of visionary themes recurred, including: darshan of Baba matching the specific golden murti/pratima installed at Ashaeiynn; darshan of Bhagwan Ram, Krishna (Kanhaiya ji), Brahma ji, and Vishnu ji; darshan of Hanuman ji specifically marked by his eyes and a white tika; darshan of a lion (Simha); visions of countless sants seated "pillar upon pillar" on
trees; visions of fellow sangat members' own sookshma shariras seated in front of Bhaiya; and visions of devtas actively placing of ferings into a havan kund.
5. The Tulsi-Replanting Vision as a Symbol of Seed-Planting (Beejar opan)

One practitioner (Snehal Jagade) described a specific vision of a dried tulsi plant being uprooted from its original pot and replanted, root and all, into a dif ferent pot — understood by the practitioner as a symbolic representation of the beejar opan (seed-planting) of Siya Tattva actively occurring within them during this stage of the sadhna track.
6. Harshit Srivastava's Account: Baba's Voice as "Ram"

Harshit Srivastava reported an especially moving experience in which repeating the word "Ram" during jaap felt as though Baba himself were speaking the word on his behalf rather than Harshit producing the sound himself. He described being moved to tears of joy , expressing deep gratitude that his family (naming his wife/family member Riya and his son Shubham) had been "saved" through this practice, thanking both Baba and Bhaiya directly and repeatedly .
7. The Practitioner With Four Darshans Over 1.5–2 Years

A practitioner who had been unwell for two weeks and had gone two days without any sadhna experience described initially fearing she would be unable to complete her jaap that day due to physical shivering and chattering teeth. After beginning her prayer despite this, she reported intense heat (comparing it to sitting inside a furnace) and a fourth darshan of Baba over the past 1.5–2 years — this time seeing Kanhaiya ji on the wall behind Bhaiya, with Baba's head visible just behind Kanhaiya ji.
8. Jorba's Testimony: Fr om Personal Crisis to "Jorba 2.0"

A practitioner referred to as Jorba shared an extended personal account (delivered lar gely in English): a severe life crisis around the COVID period (2019–2020) — despite having been a top academic performer , his life "toppled" to the point of nearly discontinuing his master's degree — that began to turn around after joining Ashaeiynn. He described two specific turning-point episodes: (a) a hostile external panel member at a critical job interview was unexpectedly counterbalanced by three normally-dif ficult senior professors who, for the first time in memory , actively helped him during his presentation, resulting in him getting the job; and (b) after some time in the new role, a visit for Tirupati Balaji darshan and an immediate return to an Ashaeiynn utsav marked what he calls the start of "Jorba 2.0" — a second life phase in which he became an expert and popular professor in his field.
9. Mankalwan's Account: Energy Sensations During Pratishtha

A practitioner named Mankalwan described practicing his morning sadhna sessions secretly on of fice stairwell steps in the early stages, and reported that on the specific day of a "pratishtha" (installation/consecration) process, his face and ears grew hot and he felt a strong "boom boom" ener gy sensation synchronized with his repetition of "Ram," followed by a return to normal after the session — describing the sensation as resembling a second heartbeat located in his own head.
10. The Himachal-Based Practitioner's Multi-Deity Darshan

A practitioner based in Himachal Pradesh, in his early days connected to Ashaeiynn (24 days at the time of sharing), described an especially rich sequence of darshans: on the very first day , spontaneously exclaiming "Ram Rajya hai" (this is Ram's kingdom) in response to the feeling of the practice; subsequently seeing Brahma ji, Vishnu ji, Bhaiya himself wearing full tilak and a red chola, Hanuman ji (marked by his eyes and white tika), and a lion — along with feeling persistently warm despite the genuinely cold Himachal climate around him.
1 1. Usha Charu's Extended Account: Fr om "Dust" to the Sky

A practitioner (addressed in the transcript in connection with "Usha Charu") who had been connected to Ashaeiynn for one year shared that, for the first time, she chose not to specifically pray for darshan during this Siya Tattva round, focusing instead simply on completing her jaap smoothly — and precisely then experienced an unusually vivid, extended vision: countless sants seated pillar upon pillar on trees, her fellow sangat members' own sookshma shariras seated before Bhaiya, ener gy and portals visibly emer ging from the havan in front of Bhaiya, an intense pull "from the heart" that she could not resist even when trying to look away , uncontrollable weeping, being progressively drawn inward into white and orange light, visible divine protection and a shower of flowers around Bhaiya, and — for the first time — actually witnessing devtas placing of ferings into the havan kund rather than only hearing this described by others. She closed by reflecting on her broader one-year journey with Ashaeiynn as a transformation from feeling like "dust" to steadily "reaching the sky ."
12. Batodia ji's Account: Reaching Shunya in the Third Charan

A practitioner named Batodia ji, roughly a month and a half into his sadhna practice, reported that his very second sadhna session already involved being given third charan (third-stage) jaap by Gurudev's grace. He described this jaap as repeatedly pulling him into a state of "shunya" (void/emptiness) accompanied by a distinct kind of bliss, which he interpreted as being drawn toward samadhi — to the point that his wife, sitting beside him, assumed he had fallen asleep. He confirmed with his mentor ("Shree Bhaiya") that he had not been sleeping but had gone into a genuinely deep state. He is currently on his fourth Siya Tattva session.
13. Batodia ji's First Workplace Account: The EUDR Rubber Certification

Batodia ji, who manages procurement (as an HOD of Materials) for his company , described a specific work crisis: a new European Union regulation (EUDR) required exported rubber products to be EUDR-certified. Rather than resorting to costlier imports, his team sought EUDR-certified rubber domestically via the Rubber Board, and his director gave him a one-week deadline (by Friday) to secure the required geo-location certification file. Batodia ji prayed to Gurudev for help; the Rubber Board confirmed and produced the required file online by Wednesday — well ahead of the Friday deadline — leaving his director impressed and asking how it had happened so quickly .
14. Batodia ji's Second Workplace Account: The Toluene/Hexene Supply Crisis

In a separate incident, Batodia ji's company's usual supplier (BPCL) suf fered a production failure and could not supply toluene, threatening a three-to-four -day production breakdown. After Batodia ji prayed to Gurudev for guidance, he received a distinct internal prompt to consider import/export sourcing despite his assistant general manager's objection that it would be roughly five times more expensive. Batodia ji describes this leading to a favorable outcome on two fronts: he secured an alternative source at a lower price than BPCL's usual rate, and — the very next day — BPCL itself also managed to supply a tanker after all, resolving the shortage from both directions simultaneously .
15. The Closing Doha: "Jaki Rahi Bhavna Jaisi"

Bhaiya closes the session by referencing the well-known doha "jaki rahi bhavna jaisi, prabhu murat dekhi tinhu taisi" (loosely: a person perceives the divine in the form shaped by their own inner feeling/faith) as the framework for understanding why dif ferent practitioners in the very same sadhna track reported darshan of dif ferent deities and forms (Ram, Krishna, Brahma, Vishnu, Hanuman, a lion, and so on) — each vision is understood as shaped by that individual's own bhavna (devotional disposition), rather than there being one single "correct" form that everyone should expect to see.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY
This session's Siya Tattva sadhna is a multi-part sequential practice track — practitioners are explicitly on their third or fourth session within it, not a single standalone exercise.

Common physical sensations reported during this stage of sadhna include intense heat/warmth (even in cold weather), a pulsing sensation in the head, and pre-breakthrough shivering that resolves once prayer/jaap begins. Common visionary themes include darshan of Baba (matching Ashaeiynn's own murti), Ram, Krishna, Brahma ji, Vishnu ji, Hanuman ji (marked by his eyes and white tika), a lion, countless sants, fellow sangat members' sookshma shariras, and devtas placing of ferings into the havan kund. A dried-tulsi-replanted vision was interpreted as a symbol of "beejaropan" (seed-planting) of Siya Tattva occurring within the practitioner . Reaching a state of "shunya"/deep absorption during third-charan jaap, sometimes mistaken by onlookers for sleep, was confirmed by a mentor as genuine deep samadhi. Practitioners reported not only inner spiritual experiences but also tangible real-world outcomes attributed to Gurudev's guidance, including two specific professional/business situations resolved favorably and unusually quickly . The closing teaching — "jaki rahi bhavna jaisi, prabhu murat dekhi tinhu taisi" — explains why dif ferent practitioners in the same practice see dif ferent divine forms: each darshan is shaped by that individual's own devotional disposition. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines

Present these accounts as first-person testimonies shared live by named practitioners, not as independently verified claims or universal guarantees of what any practitioner will experience. Keep the "jaki rahi bhavna jaisi" framing intact when a user asks why dif ferent practitioners see dif ferent deities during similar practices — this is this teaching's own explicit explanation, not an inconsistency to resolve. Present the workplace/professional outcomes (Batodia ji's two accounts) as personal testimony of perceived guidance, not as a guarantee of specific material outcomes for any practitioner who prays similarly .

Keep individual practitioners' accounts attributed to them specifically (e.g., do not mer ge Harshit Srivastava's account with Usha Charu's, or Batodia ji's samadhi account with his workplace accounts) — these are distinct testimonies from distinct people. Note that this session's Siya Tattva sadhna is explicitly a multi-part, sequential track (third/fourth sessions referenced), not a single standalone practice. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 68, Hinglish)
Siya Tattva Sadhna ke Anubhav — Sangat ki Apni Kahaniyaan

Note on this session's format: Yeh poora session hi structurally ek live experience-sharing r ound hai — Bhaiya ki traditional teaching ke bajaye, sangat member ek-ek karke apne Siya T attva sadhna ke anubhav shar e karte hain. Isliye yahan Part III "curated" hai bajaye "exhaustive" ke — kyunki poora transcript hi conversational hai, sirf sabse vivid, emotionally r esonant, aur genuinely valuable anubhav chune gaye hain, har ek ke saath ek italicized rationale note. Baaki sabhi individual anubhav Part I (Knowledge Base) mein alr eady summarize ho chuke hain.

Yeh exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh poor e session ka natural, unifying closing hai — ek classical doha ke thr ough Bhaiya samjhate hain ki alag-alag practitioners ne alag-alag devi-devta kyun dekhe, aur yeh ek r espectful, non-hierar chical note pe session ko band karta hai jahan har ek ka anubhav apni jagah valid hai.
